result:
None of the three solutions is correct, but Solution 1 is the least wrong.

**Reformulation.** Each root is obtained by starting at 0 and applying the maps $y \mapsto y/4+\alpha$, $y\mapsto y/6+\beta$, $y\mapsto y/9+\gamma$ in some order of length 20, where $\alpha=-a/4$, $\beta=-b/6$, $\gamma=-c/9$. Let $V_n$ be the set of values after $n$ steps, so $R=|V_{20}|$.

**Solution 1 (21) is impossible.** If $V_{n-1}$ has at least two points, then $|V_n| \ge |V_{n-1}|+1$. Equality would force $L_f(V_{n-1})=L_g(V_{n-1})$ as sets, but these have spreads $D/4$ and $D/6$, so $D=0$, a contradiction. Also, if $|V_1|=2$, the three images cannot fit in a 3-point set, because $1/4 \neq 1/6+1/9$, $1/6 \neq 1/4+1/9$, and $1/9 \neq 1/4+1/6$. So $|V_2|\ge 4$ whenever $V_1$ is not a singleton. Then $|V_{20}| \ge 4+18 = 22$. The singleton case gives $3^{19}$. So $R=21$ cannot occur.

**Solution 2 (3^19) is not the second smallest.** Take $a=3$, $b=5$, $c=8$. Then $f,g,h$ all fix $x=-1$, so a composition with slope $M=4^p6^q9^r$ has root $1/M-1$. Distinct roots correspond to distinct $M$. Writing $M=2^{2p+q}3^{q+2r}$ with $p+q+r=20$, the exponent $2p+q$ takes every value in $\{0,\dots,40\}$, giving exactly $41$ distinct values. Since $41<3^{19}$, the value $3^{19}$ cannot be the second smallest.

**Solution 3 ($(3^{20}+1)/2$) fails for the same reason.** It is far larger than the 41 achieved above.

I have not established that 41 is the true answer. A configuration giving a value between 22 and 40 may exist, and I did not rule that out.

CHOICE: 1
